rules.title: Java 9 and 10 are no longer supported
rules.summary: The Oracle Java SE Support Roadmap lists Java 9 and 10 as non-LTS releases whose Premier Support ended between March 2018 and September 2018. It says a previous non-LTS release is superseded once a new feature release is made available.

constraints: Keep the JDK in the build files, the version pin files, CI, and container images on one supported release; a long-term-support release avoids repeating this migration every six months.
Check that the Gradle or Maven version in the project can run on the target JDK (the Gradle compatibility matrix lists the supported Java versions).
A compile level (`maven.compiler.release`, `sourceCompatibility`) is not the JDK that runs the code: lower it only if the code must still run on an older runtime.

steps.title: Move the reported declaration to a supported JDK
steps.instructions: Change the reported version to a long-term-support release (see the replacement) in the build file or the version pin file.

steps.title: Align the other JDK declarations
steps.instructions: Update every other pom.xml, Gradle toolchain, `.java-version`, `.sdkmanrc`, `.tool-versions`, CI JDK setup, and container base image that names the old release, so the repository agrees.

verification.purpose: Build and test the project on the new JDK with the wrapper the project uses.
Confirm the JDK on the path (or the one the toolchain selects) is the intended release.

rules.title: mysql:mysql-connector-java has moved to com.mysql:mysql-connector-j
rules.summary: The POM of mysql:mysql-connector-java 8.0.33 declares a relocation to com.mysql:mysql-connector-j. Its message says: "MySQL Connector/J artifacts moved to reverse-DNS compliant Maven 2+ coordinates."

constraints: Replace mysql:mysql-connector-java with com.mysql:mysql-connector-j; the relocation in the artifact's POM names the new coordinates, so keep the version unless you intend to upgrade it.
Update every module and dependency-management block that names the old coordinates, and remove exclusions that mention them.

steps.title: Change the dependency coordinates
steps.instructions: Replace the reported `mysql:mysql-connector-java` dependency with `com.mysql:mysql-connector-j`.

steps.title: Align other declarations
steps.instructions: Update every other pom.xml, Gradle build file, version catalog, and BOM override that names the old coordinates.

verification.purpose: Confirm the old coordinates are gone from the resolved dependency graph.
Build and test the project with the new coordinates.

rules.title: Spring Boot 1.x is out of open-source support
rules.summary: Spring Boot 1.x has reached the end of its open-source support lifecycle. Upgrade to a supported Spring Boot 4.x line; assess the 1.x-to-4.x migration in stages because it crosses multiple major releases. Commercial support availability is separate from community OSS support.

constraints: This finding describes open-source support, not whether a commercial support contract exists.
Do not jump directly across several major versions without reviewing each intervening migration guide and compatibility requirements.

steps.title: Plan the major-version upgrade
steps.instructions: Inventory Spring Boot, Spring Framework, Java, build-tool, and managed dependency versions. Read each Spring Boot migration guide between the current version and the selected 4.x target.

steps.title: Align Spring Boot declarations
steps.instructions: Update the Spring Boot dependency, parent/BOM, plugin, and related build declarations consistently, then resolve and remove obsolete configuration using the migration guides.

verification.purpose: Build and run the project's tests after the staged upgrade.
Review the resolved Spring dependency graph for mixed or obsolete versions.

rules.title: Spring Boot 2.x is out of open-source support
rules.summary: Spring Boot 2.x no longer receives regular open-source releases. Spring Boot 2.7 had an extended commercial support period, which is distinct from community OSS support. Upgrade to a supported Spring Boot 4.x line and follow the 2.x-to-3.x and 3.x-to-4.x migration guidance.

constraints: Spring Boot 2.7's extended commercial support does not mean the 2.x line remains in community open-source support.
Spring Boot 3 requires Java 17 or later and includes the Jakarta EE namespace migration; complete the 2.x-to-3.x changes before moving to 4.x.

steps.title: Upgrade to a supported 3.x baseline first
steps.instructions: Follow the official Spring Boot 3 migration guide, move to Java 17 or later, and migrate Java EE javax APIs to their Jakarta equivalents where required.

steps.title: Move to a supported 4.x release
steps.instructions: Follow the Spring Boot 4 migration guide, align Spring Framework and managed dependencies, and remove configuration deprecated by the intermediate releases.

verification.purpose: Build and run the project's tests after the upgrade.
Check that the resolved dependency graph uses a consistent supported Spring Boot line.

rules.title: Spring Boot 3.x is out of open-source support
rules.summary: Spring Boot 3.x has reached the end of its open-source support lifecycle. The 3.3.x and 3.4.x lines were explicitly marked as the end of OSS support, and 3.5.16 was announced as the last OSS release of the 3.5.x generation. Commercial support may be available separately. Upgrade to a supported 4.x line.

sources.title: Spring Boot 3.3.13 — end of open-source support
Spring Boot 3.4.13 — end of open-source support
Spring Boot 3.5.16 — last OSS release of the 3.5.x generation

constraints: Spring Boot 4 requires Java 17 or later; verify the selected build tool and all third-party starters support the target line.
Read the Spring Boot 4 migration guide for removed APIs and dependency changes rather than treating this as a version-only bump.

steps.title: Update Spring Boot to a supported 4.x line
steps.instructions: Update the parent/BOM, direct Spring Boot dependencies, and Spring Boot build plugin to the same supported 4.x release.

steps.title: Apply the 4.x migration guide
steps.instructions: Resolve migration changes for Spring Framework, Jakarta APIs, auto-configuration, and third-party starters; remove obsolete settings and keep dependency management aligned.

verification.purpose: Build and test the application against the selected Spring Boot 4.x release.
Confirm Spring Boot and Spring Framework dependencies resolve to a compatible 4.x stack.
